what_its_for: Riociguat is used to treat two types of high blood pressure that affect the lungs and heart: pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) and chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH). It works by relaxing and widening the blood vessels in your lungs, making it easier for your heart to pump blood and helping you breathe more easily and exercise more comfortably.
how_to_take: Take riociguat by mouth 3 times a day, about 6 to 8 hours apart. You can take it with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole or crush it and mix with water or soft foods like applesauce if you have trouble swallowing. Try to take it at the same times each day to keep a steady amount in your body. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first, as stopping suddenly can make your condition worse.
dosing: Your doctor will usually start you on a low dose of 1 mg three times a day and slowly increase your dose every 2 weeks based on how you respond and how well you tolerate the medication. The maximum dose is 2.5 mg three times a day. Never change your dose on your own — always follow your doctor's instructions exactly.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is more than 2 hours before your next scheduled dose. If your next dose is coming up in less than 2 hours, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store riociguat tablets at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep them away from moisture, heat, and direct light. Store the tablets in their original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep this medication out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medication after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Do not take riociguat if you are pregnant or may become pregnant — it can cause serious harm or death to an unborn baby. Women must use two reliable forms of birth control while taking this medicine and during treatment through the ADEMPAS REMS Program. Avoid nitrates (like nitroglycerin) and drugs called PDE-5 inhibitors (like sildenafil, tadalafil, or vardenafil) — taking these together with riociguat can cause a dangerous drop in blood pressure. Avoid smoking, as it reduces how well this medicine works. Limit alcohol use, as it can lower your blood pressure too much. Be careful when standing up quickly, as riociguat can cause dizziness. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice, as it may affect how the drug works in your body.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: severe dizziness or fainting, signs of very low blood pressure (feeling lightheaded, blurry vision, unusual weakness), coughing up blood or bloody mucus, shortness of breath that gets worse suddenly, signs of bleeding (unusual bruising, blood in urine or stool), or if you think you might be pregnant. Also call your doctor before starting any new medications, including supplements or over-the-counter drugs.
when_it_works: You may start to notice improvements in your ability to exercise and breathe within a few weeks of starting treatment. However, it may take several weeks to a few months to feel the full benefit of this medication. This drug helps manage your condition but does not cure it, so it is important to keep taking it every day as directed even if you feel well.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Riociguat must NOT be used during pregnancy. It can cause miscarriage, stillbirth, or serious birth defects. All women who can become pregnant must be enrolled in a special safety program called the ADEMPAS REMS Program, have a negative pregnancy test before starting, and use two forms of birth control during treatment. Breastfeeding: Do not breastfeed while taking this medication. Elderly patients (65 and older): May be more sensitive to blood pressure-lowering effects; use with caution and close monitoring. Kidney or liver problems: Dose adjustments may be needed; let your doctor know about any kidney or liver conditions before starting this medication. Children: Riociguat is not approved for use in children under 18 years of age.
